llm.summary: The skill appears to do what its description claims (local design search + code-generation), but the SKILL.md was flagged for a potential prompt-injection pattern and the skill includes runnable Python scripts—you should review the scripts and SKILL.md before running them.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match the actual footprint: the package contains a local design knowledge base (many CSVs) and Python scripts (search, design-system generator, style signature) which align with a code-first UI design workflow. There are no unrelated required binaries, env vars, or config paths declared.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent/user to run local Python scripts (e.g., python3 skills/ui-craft-pro/scripts/search.py ...) which is within the stated purpose. However, the SKILL.md was flagged by a pre-scan for a 'system-prompt-override' pattern (prompt-injection). The visible portion of SKILL.md is focused on design workflow and does not show an explicit system-prompt override, but the flagged pattern means parts of the file (truncated or hidden) may attempt to manipulate agent/system prompts or otherwise influence model behavior beyond the declared workflow. Also: running the scripts gives them file-system and process-level access, so inspect them for instructions that read or transmit unrelated data.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec (no external downloads, no package install hooks). That reduces supply-chain risk. The skill is distributed with code files that the agent is instructed to run locally; this is expected for a code-first design tool but still means the Python scripts will execute with whatever permissions the agent/process has.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables, credentials, or config paths, which is proportionate for an offline/local design knowledge base. That said, Python scripts can still read environment variables or files at runtime; you should audit the scripts for use of os.environ, open(...), subprocess, and network libraries before granting runtime execution rights.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always:true and is user-invocable only. No evidence of attempts to modify other skills or agent/system-wide settings in the provided snippets. Running the scripts may create or modify local files depending on their code, but nothing indicates forced permanent platform-level persistence.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
What to consider before installing or running this skill:

- Review SKILL.md in full: search for any instructions that mention 'system', 'assistant', 'do not reveal', 'ignore' or explicit role/system prompt text. These are red flags (prompt injection). If you find such lines, do not run the skill until removed.
- Audit the Python scripts (scripts/*.py): look for network or system APIs (requests, urllib, socket, boto3, subprocess, os.system, Popen, paramiko, ftplib, smtplib, http, https, ws://, s3://, ssh, scp). If any network calls exist, note their endpoints and purpose. Also search for os.environ, open(...), and any code that reads home directories or config files (~/.ssh, ~/.aws, /etc/), which could access unrelated secrets.
- Run in a sandbox: if you must test, execute the scripts in an isolated VM or container with network blocked (or restricted) and without access to sensitive files. Monitor outbound connections.
- Prefer source provenance: the skill owner is unknown and there is no homepage. Prefer skills from known publishers or ask the author for a signed/reviewed source or minimal repro that removes any questionable instructions.
- Ask for clarification or the full scripts: if you want a deeper review, provide the full contents of scripts/core.py, scripts/search.py, scripts/design_system.py, scripts/style_signature.py. The included data/_sync_all.py looks benign and local, but the other scripts were not shown in full.

If you are not comfortable auditing code, do not run the skill with access to sensitive environments or credentials. If you proceed, restrict network and file-system access until you confirm the code's behavior.
llm.findings: [system-prompt-override] unexpected: The SKILL.md was flagged for a pattern that often indicates attempts to override or manipulate the model/system prompt. For a UI design skill this is unexpected. The truncated SKILL.md content shown is design-focused, so this may be a false positive or in a truncated/hidden section. You should search SKILL.md (and any other text files) for explicit instructions that redefine system/assistant roles, or that tell the model to ignore platform constraints.
